# Teewald

> Teewald is a free third-person survival horror game with a PlayStation 1 look that runs right in the web browser (PC, phone and tablet). It is set in Teewald, a fictional small town of German settlers in the hills of southern Brazil, inspired by Santa Maria do Herval (Rio Grande do Sul). In May 1997, deep in autumn and fog, livestock turns up dead with two holes in the neck and not a drop of blood, and a stranger decides to stay and find out what walks in the woods.

- Play: https://fabianokunst.github.io/Teewald-3d/?lang=en (free, nothing to install, no account needed)
- Official site: https://fabianokunst.github.io/Teewald-3d/site/en/
- Creator: Fabiano Kunst (indie game)
- Genre: survival horror / third-person horror, single player, twelve chapters, each built around a legend from the Brazilian countryside
- Gameplay: over-the-shoulder camera, scarce ammo, punches and melee weapons that wear out and break, 9 mm pistol, dodge, 16-slot inventory, documents to read (FILES), conversations with 24 townsfolk, three difficulty levels and an S-to-C rank for each chapter
- Visuals: CLEAN 3D (default) or RETRO PS1 (320×240, dithering and 15-bit color); weather with late afternoon, night, fog, rain and storms; all sound generated in code
- Platforms: any up-to-date browser with WebGL (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari) on PC, phone and tablet
- Controls: keyboard and mouse, controller (USB or Bluetooth, with aim assist and vibration) or touch screen
- Languages: Portuguese, English, Spanish and German
- Progress: saved automatically in the browser itself
- Setting: streets, river and terrain from open data (OpenStreetMap, Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints and SRTM), with about 600 buildings on their real footprints
- Technology: Three.js (WebGL) and Vite

A work of fiction: Teewald was born of imagination. The characters, their names, the dialogue and everything that happens in the game are made up, and any resemblance to real persons, living or dead, or to real events is purely coincidental. Santa Maria do Herval (RS) served only as inspiration for the setting: the street layout and street names, the river, the terrain and a few places come from public maps and appear only as scenery. The game does not portray the town, its residents, businesses or institutions, and has no connection whatsoever with the City Hall or any organization in the municipality.

No spoilers: the site only tells what the player hears and reads right after arriving in town. The creatures of each chapter and what happens after the first night are left for the game.

## Site pages

- [Home](https://fabianokunst.github.io/Teewald-3d/site/en/index.html.md): Third-person survival horror with a PlayStation 1 look, set in a small town of German settlers in the hills of southern Brazil. Free, in your browser.
- [The story](https://fabianokunst.github.io/Teewald-3d/site/en/historia.html.md): Teewald, the tea woods: a colony of immigrants from the Hunsrück in the Herval Valley. May 1997, fog, and livestock turning up dead without a drop of blood.
- [The town](https://fabianokunst.github.io/Teewald-3d/site/en/cidade.html.md): The places of Teewald: the Rio Cadeia promenade, Praça 10 de Abril, the parish church, the Kartoffelfest pavilion, the half-timbered houses and the woods. A town made from real maps.
- [Characters](https://fabianokunst.github.io/Teewald-3d/site/en/personagens.html.md): The characters of Teewald: the stranger and the 24 townsfolk who talk, with each one’s portrait, height, clothes and manner, taken from the game’s models.
- [The game](https://fabianokunst.github.io/Teewald-3d/site/en/jogo.html.md): How to play Teewald: combat, inventory, files, the CLEAN 3D and RETRO PS1 visual styles, weather, keyboard, controller and touch controls, and frequently asked questions.
- [Gallery](https://fabianokunst.github.io/Teewald-3d/site/en/galeria.html.md): Screenshots of Teewald taken from the game itself: the parish church, the square at night, the Rio Cadeia promenade, the Kartoffelfest, rain, fog and the RETRO PS1 look.

## Game

- [Teewald in the browser](https://fabianokunst.github.io/Teewald-3d/?lang=en): the game itself (WebGL; the page has no text to read without running the game). This link opens the game in English; `?lang=pt`, `?lang=es` or `?lang=de` in the address forces another language.
